newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Borotra says lira still undervalued.
newsitem.headline: France's Borotra says lira still undervalued.

text.p: French industry minister Franck Borotra said on Monday that the Italian lira was still undervalued.
"For the Italians, the lira has regained its right value, but for the French that is not the case," Borotra told a chamber of commerce meeting.
"The devaluation of the lira has left very important scars on our industrial landscape. If you ask me whether the lira has regained its right value, the answer is 'no'," he said.
Borotra said he expected European authorities to accept French state aid to industrial sectors particularly hit by "unfair competition" following the lira's devaluation.
He singled out the textile industry in particular.
French President Jacques Chirac touched off a diplomatic row last week when he blamed the problems of the country's textile industry on unfair competition from a weak lira.

Chirac questioned at the time Italy's fitness to be a founding member of Europe's planned single currency but later rowed back from the comments after a meeting with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
Prodi said during the weekend the French government had not asked Italy to encourage a further appreciation of the lira before seeking the currency's re-enty into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism.
In his speech, Borotra also called for a common European industrial policy to face "the challenge of America and the threat of Asia".
